test_policy.notes: Test-optional: SAT/ACT are the applicant's choice. The exception is an English proficiency test, which may be required depending on native language and the curriculum of the applicant's high school.

requirements.notes: Apply with the Common App or the MCPHS Application. The Common App grid lists a $50 fee for U.S. and international applicants and accepts fee waivers; the fee for the MCPHS Application was not confirmed on mcphs.edu. Required: official high school transcript from the counselor or school (algebra 1 and 2 and geometry, biology and chemistry, 4 years of English, 1 year of history) and one letter of recommendation from a counselor or teacher (math or science preferred). The Common App grid lists the personal essay as required; no interview requirement was found.

deadlines.label: Early Action Round I (priority filing date, fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: International applications are accepted on a rolling basis with these priority filing dates; a decision is made only once the file is complete. Notification mid-December (first-year page). The pages print no year; taken as the 2026-27 cycle.

deadlines.label: Early Action Round II (priority filing date)
Regular Decision (priority filing date)
deadlines.notes: Notification mid-February (first-year page). Admission is rolling and MCPHS promises a status update within three weeks of receiving all materials; no hard closing date is published.

deadlines.label: Enrollment deposit
deadlines.notes: Confirm through the online deposit gateway by May 1; if admitted after May 1, within two weeks. The enrollment deposit is $500-$750 (tuition page).

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required if English is not the primary spoken language. May be waived individually for applicants with 4 years of US high school (excluding ESL), SAT Evidence-based Reading/Writing 480+ (ACT English 21 is also listed as proof), 4 years at a US-accredited high school abroad, IB or A2-level curriculum, or a US bachelor's degree or higher. A completion certificate from an agreement ESL school can replace a test score. Three admission types: direct, conditional (for applicants who still need to take a test or more English study) and bridge. The Academic Bridge Program is a one-semester pathway for academically admissible students with about TOEFL 69-78 (or equivalent): two major courses plus three academic English courses, then progression to full-time degree study; entry in September or January for most programs; tuition equals a regular bachelor's semester. Optional Early Start Program for new international undergraduates (about 10 days in August, Aug. 12-21 in 2026; $300 fee).

english.notes: Bridge admission minimum 69. Also accepted: TOEFL ITP 550 (bridge 498), iTEP 4.0 (bridge 3.7), SAT ERW 480 or ACT English 21. The page gives no new 1-6 TOEFL score.

aid.notes: International page: all first-year applicants are reviewed for merit scholarships at acceptance with no separate application; no award amounts are published. Need-based federal aid is described only for eligible noncitizens (permanent residents, refugees, etc.), and the institutional need-based MCPHS Award is based on the FAFSA, so F-1 students appear not to qualify (inferred, not stated). Government-sponsored students must submit a financial guarantee letter. Annual health insurance is $4,364 (waivable); Flywire is used for international payments.

cost.notes: Boston undergraduate bachelor-degree tuition is $43,110 per academic year for 2026-27 (3-year accelerated programs $62,480; PharmD preprofessional phase also $43,110, professional phase $51,900). Other mandatory fees: comprehensive service fee $705 billed fall and spring (6+ credits), orientation fee $175, graduation fee $390. room_board_usd is the school's estimated Boston budget for housing $18,990 + food $5,940 (traditional year); other_usd is transportation $1,564 + miscellaneous $1,822. Residence hall rates vary (about $9,300-$9,750 per semester). The tuition page lists one rate; there is no separate international rate.

majors.notes: Direct-entry six-year program: first-year students are admitted into the PharmD (two preprofessional years, then four professional years). To progress to year 3 students need a 2.8 GPA by the end of year 2, preprofessional courses at C- or better, a PharmCAS application, an oral interview and a written assessment; then a 2.7 cumulative GPA in years 3-6 (2025-26 catalog).

Year I fall includes BIO 110, CHE 110 and ITM 101 (catalog curriculum). Students must pass the ATI TEAS with 65.3 or higher within three attempts before entering the professional nursing curriculum and keep a professional GPA of 2.7. Clinical placement capacity is not published.
School of Arts and Sciences; tracks include Clinical Research, Regulatory Affairs and Health Policy, and Pharmacology (catalog).
Tracks listed in the catalog include Optometry, Osteopathic Medicine, Physician Assistant Studies and Veterinary Medicine.
School of Healthcare Business and Technology (catalog).

tier_notes.general: Admit rate about 85%, but a health-sciences-focused private university in Boston with direct-entry programs (6-year PharmD, accelerated BSN); SAT section medians of 610 ERW / 645 Math among the few (7%) who submit. Editorial judgment, wave 3 (2026-10-26).
